# uzys-agent-harness

> A harness that helps your AI coding agent work smarter, and work better as models improve. One command installs the rules and skills for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Antigravity. Install with `npx -y @uzysjung/agent-harness` (interactive wizard; Node.js 20.12 or newer) or `npx -y @uzysjung/agent-harness install --track <name>` (non-interactive; `--track` is the only required flag). MIT.

The problem: if you have kept adding rules to Claude Code or Codex, the instruction file keeps growing and the agent misses more and more of it. Even when a new model ships, the rules you wrote to stop the old model's mistakes get in its way. uzys-agent-harness doesn't tie the agent down with a list of rules. It builds the agent's working environment on four ideas:

1. As models get better, the harness gets better with them. Instead of piling up dos and don'ts, it tells the agent what to base its judgment on and which lines it must not cross. For example, instead of "add tests to every change," it says "decide how deeply to verify based on the change's impact and the cost of undoing it." Instructions for things the model now does well on its own come out, so when a new model arrives, the agent can use what it can do instead of being held back by old rules.
2. With a direction and limits, the agent goes further on its own. Before work is handed over, the project's direction, the task's definition of done, and the lines not to cross are set first. With those to check against, the agent tries, checks its work, and fixes it, again and again, on its own. It can work longer without step-by-step direction, and it is told to ask you only about the decisions that are yours.
3. The harness stays light. Every instruction the agent reads each session takes up context, and as they pile up the important ones get buried. So only short rules are read every session, and longer procedures are opened only when needed. Each release drops what is no longer useful, and you can find and drop stale instructions in your own project too.
4. Several viewpoints and several agents balance speed, cost, and quality. The agent that built something doesn't judge its own work. Review goes to another agent, and when it helps, the work is examined through several users' eyes or a model from another vendor gives a second opinion. Each task gets a fitting model and reasoning effort: light work fast and cheap, important work done carefully.

What you get: one command installs the rules and skills that carry these four ideas, plus third-party skills for your stack (from official repositories or ones that passed this project's vetting). Your `CLAUDE.md` gets one marked block and nothing else is touched; uninstalling removes only what the harness added. Works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Antigravity; hooks and the reviewer agent run on Claude Code.

## Install it now

- Run `npx -y @uzysjung/agent-harness` in your project folder (Node.js 20.12 or newer).
- The wizard asks five things: 1 Tracks (your stack; items that fit it are pre-checked), 2 CLI (one or more of claude / codex / opencode / antigravity), 3 Install items (review the pre-checked items; drop or add anything), 4 Confirm (a summary, and how many tokens your selection adds per session), 5 Installing.
- Picking a stack pre-checks the rules, skills, and external tools that fit it. That is only a recommendation: at step 3 you decide everything that goes in or stays out, and you can pick more than one stack. Without the wizard, `--with <id>` and `--without <id>` make the same choices.
- Then open your AI coding tool in the same folder (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, or `agy`). The rules and skills apply from the first session.
- First thing to do: the install adds blank sections about your project to `CLAUDE.md` (or `AGENTS.md`). Tell your agent once: "Use the audit-harness-fit skill to read the code and fill in the project sections." Say the same thing later to check whether the setup still fits your project.
- No terminal for the wizard (CI, containers, scripts)? The only required flag is `install --track <name>`. Claude Code plugins need the `claude` command on your PATH; without it they are skipped with a warning.

## In detail

How the principles are built in:

- Judgment criteria, not checklists. A typical rule says "Add unit tests for every change and get a review before every commit." This harness's working principles say "Choose the depth, timing, and combination of testing, review, and release checks according to actual impact, uncertainty, recovery cost, and existing evidence." Under the first, fixing a typo takes the same steps as changing billing logic; the second gives the model a reason to treat them differently. It doesn't mean testing less.
- Goal and finish line first. The `north-star` skill records what the project is for and what it won't do; the `objective-brief` skill does the same for each task (goal, completion criteria, boundaries). Methods are not fixed.
- Limits come with reasons, and very few are enforced. Destructive actions, deployments, and writes to anything other people share need your approval when they go beyond the work you handed over. Only two things are enforced mechanically: on Claude Code, a hook blocks edits to `.env`, lock files, and certificates, and a bundled script puts protection rules on your GitHub default branch.
- What the model now does well comes out of the instructions. Before you install, the wizard shows how many tokens your selection adds to every session. After you install, the `audit-harness-fit` skill finds instructions your project no longer needs and suggests what to change.
- The agent that builds is not the one that checks. On Claude Code, a `reviewer` subagent that didn't write the code runs your tests or the app and checks the result. With the optional `model-orchestration` skill, the agent also picks the model and reasoning effort for each task.

What gets installed (Claude Code, dev track): `CLAUDE.md` (yours; one harness block added at the end), `CLAUDE-uzys-harness.md` (working principles read every session), `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/` (reviewer, implementer), `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings.json` (merged with yours), `.mcp.json` (merged with yours), and `.uzys-agent-harness/` (the install record and helper scripts). All of it stays inside your project; commit it and teammates who clone the repo get the same setup. Every track gets `north-star`, `objective-brief`, `gh-issue-workflow`, and `audit-harness-fit`.

What each tool gets: Claude Code gets rules, skills, hooks, subagents, and plugins. Codex gets rules (in `AGENTS.md`), skills, and the session-start hook only. OpenCode gets rules (in `AGENTS.md`) and skills. Antigravity gets rules and skills. Plugins are a Claude Code feature, so only Claude Code gets them.

Supported stacks (tracks): `base`, `csr-supabase`, `csr-fastify`, `csr-fastapi`, `ssr-nextjs`, `ssr-htmx`, `data`, `tooling`, `full`, `executive`, `project-management`, `growth-marketing`. Each pre-checks external skills from an official repository or one that passed this project's vetting; every track gets the `context7`, `github`, and `chrome-devtools` MCP servers. More external assets are never pre-checked but can be added at step 3 or with `--with <id>`.

Main commands: `list` shows what this project got; `update` brings it to the current release (refreshes what the harness installed, adds what a newer release introduced, puts back harness files that went missing, never installs a tool you did not choose); `uninstall` removes everything, one tool (`--cli`), or single assets (`--only`), with `--dry-run` to preview, and never deletes `.claude/`, `.codex/`, or `.opencode/` (each is moved aside as `<dir>.backup-<ts>`). A teammate who clones a repo set up with the harness has nothing to do: the install record is committed with the files. Before replacing a file you edited, the harness writes a timestamped backup next to it; existing `.mcp.json` servers are merged, not replaced. Nothing goes to `~/.opencode/`, `~/.gemini/`, or global npm; two opt-in exceptions write outside the project (the Claude Code plugin cache under `~/.claude/plugins/`, and `--with-codex-trust`, one trust entry in `~/.codex/config.toml`).

Already using something else: if you write your own `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, keep it; the harness adds one marked block and adds what a single file can't (a hook that actually blocks, a reviewer separate from the agent that builds, an install record so `update` and `uninstall` touch only what the harness put there). If you pick skills from a marketplace and need only one, take just that one with `npx skills add uzysjung/uzys-agent-harness --skill <id> -a claude-code`. If you use another harness with many rules: fewer standing instructions here, with their per-session token cost shown before you install; for a fixed process, add `openspec` or `bmad-method` (both optional).

- [Tracks](https://github.com/uzysjung/uzys-agent-harness/blob/main/docs/TRACKS.md): what each track pre-checks

- [Which file is whose](https://github.com/uzysjung/uzys-agent-harness/blob/main/docs/CONTEXT-FILES.md): `CLAUDE.md`, the anchor, `AGENTS.md`, and the other context files
- [Workflows](https://github.com/uzysjung/uzys-agent-harness/blob/main/docs/WORKFLOWS.md): the opt-in workflow bundles compared, and when you don't need one

- [North Star](https://github.com/uzysjung/uzys-agent-harness/blob/main/docs/NORTH_STAR.md) and [decisions](https://github.com/uzysjung/uzys-agent-harness/blob/main/docs/decisions/): why the harness is shaped this way
